dek: A former CPA who has sold picks for about two decades under the nickname The Bulldog, first under his own Players Advantage brand, later at WagerTalk and since August 2025 at Doc's Sports. Packages run from $25 a day to $849 a season. His posted numbers are runs and seasons graded by the stores that sell him, and buyer comments we could find are few and mostly old.

short_answer: Scott Rickenbach is a real and long running pick seller. A 2010 era listing on HandicappingReviews.com described him as an independent handicapper with 12 years of experience and owner of Players Advantage, Inc. VerifiedCappers says he graduated college in 1993 and passed all four parts of the CPA exam on the first try that year. He sold through WagerTalk until 2025, and on 15 Aug 2025 Doc's Sports announced him as its newest handicapper. On 19 Nov 2026 his Doc's Sports page was live and updated that morning, while two older outlets now show "Capper not found" (BetFirm) or say he is "no longer posting picks on our platform" (Professional Sports Picks).

His numbers are hard to judge from outside. Doc's Sports shows runs such as 193-134 (+12,705) across all sports, 210-152 (+$15,430) for the 2026 MLB season and 21-12 on NHL plays of 5 units or more. We checked the win rates and they match the records, but each is a run or a slice by unit size, picked and graded by the store that sells him. A Doc's newsletter from 29 Jul 2026 gave a different all sports run, 134-109 (+5,160), about 55%. Older affiliate pages say he was ranked third, first and third in the NFL for 2012, 2013 and 2014; those percentages also match the records given.

Independent buyer comments are scarce. Two ratings on HandicappingReviews.com from 2010 and 2011 averaged 2.3 out of 5, one saying the reviewer lost more than they won in two weeks. Forum mentions are short: a 2009 TheRX exchange about chasing his hot streak, and a 2022 Freaks Forum member naming him as a favourite. TheRX in 2026 lists him among services whose plays members may not post.

guarantee: Doc's Sports uses two kinds of promise on his page. On one day packages the remedy is store credit. The NBA day package says: "If your package finishes at a loss, a $30 credit will be added to your account the following morning". The college basketball day package pays the $30 credit unless the day makes "at least $40 in profit across all plays", and the NHL day package pays it after "a loss (or profit less than $35)". The other sports day package says "We guarantee you a daily profit with this package or you will receive a $25 credit for a future purchase."

On weekly and monthly packages the remedy is more picks. The basketball and hockey packages say: "If the package finishes at a loss, you can extend your service for free through our self-extend program." The football monthly package says it is "backed by our profit guarantee, and you can use our self-extend service if we do not produce a profit." We saw no guarantee wording on the season packages.
We found no cash refund terms on his page or on the Doc's Sports contact page. Neither promise covers what you lose on the bets themselves, which is usually far more than the package price.

claims_note: Most numbers on his page are slices: a season, a run from an unstated date, or only plays rated 5, 6 or 7 units and up. Each slice can be true and still hide the full result. Ask for every play from a fixed date, at every unit size.

His length of service is told several ways. A 2010 era listing said 12 years of handicapping, VerifiedCappers said 13 years, an affiliate page said 10+ years, and Doc's Sports said 22 years in 2025. These roughly agree on a start around 1998 to 2003, but no page gives an exact date.
record: What is independently logged: nothing we could find. The outside pages we opened are affiliate or reseller pages that repeat his own figures, and two of them (BetFirm and Professional Sports Picks) now show "Capper not found" or say he is "no longer posting picks on our platform". VerifiedCappers shows no picks and no reviews.

What the store itself publishes: the Doc's Sports page lists dozens of runs and season totals. We recomputed the win rates we could and they match the records given. The size of the profit is hard to read. The 2025 announcement quotes some long term figures "at $100 per bet", but his plays are rated from about 3 to 8 units, and the page does not say how much was risked in total, so the return per dollar risked on figures such as +$15,430 over 362 MLB plays is not shown.
Doc's Sports sells his packages, grades his picks and publishes the runs, so the store and the scorekeeper are the same company.

our_data.text: In this edition no Scott Rickenbach pick is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how he performs.

customers_intro: We found very little written by buyers. The independent posts we could open are two ratings from 2010 and 2011, a short 2009 forum exchange and one 2022 forum mention. The rest are affiliate pages, the seller's own posts and forum rules.

customers.text: We found five independent posts about Scott Rickenbach across three sites, spread from 2009 to 2022. The only written buyer review, on HandicappingReviews.com in January 2011, said the reviewer lost more than they won in two weeks; a second rating from 2010 had no text, and the two together average 2.3 out of 5. On TheRX in 2009 one member warned that people who chase a capper's hot streak get burned when the numbers come back to earth, while another said they had made their biggest wins following whoever was hot, naming Rickenbach. In 2022 a Freaks Forum member listed him among favourite cappers. Nothing we found accuses him of fraud, and nothing independent confirms his records. TheRX in 2026 lists him among services whose plays members may not post, and a 2017 TheRX thread praising him came from a promotion account selling his packages.

A reviewer on HandicappingReviews.com rated results 1 out of 5. The reviewer said they lost more than they won over two weeks, that the college football and NBA picks were mostly wrong and a college basketball pick lost badly, and advised others to stay away unless they can afford to lose money.
A second reviewer on the same site left ratings only: 3 out of 5 for results, 2 for accuracy and 2 for customer service, with no written comment.

In a TheRX thread about another tout, a member said they would watch how Rickenbach did for the rest of the season, warning that bettors who chase hot streaks end up in trouble when a capper's percentages come back to earth.

Replying in the same thread, another member said they did not know Rickenbach personally but had made their biggest wins by following the cappers who were hot at the time, and named Rickenbach as one of them.
In a Freaks Forum thread titled "Your favorite handicapper?", a member listed Scott Rickenbach among the cappers they like, while criticising some cappers at other services. No results were given.

A TheRX account titled for handicapping service tracking, which promoted paid packages, posted that Rickenbach finished January at the top of its yearly leaderboard with over $34,000 profit for $1,000 a game clients, and offered his 7 day package at $174.99 and 30 day package at $399.99. This is advertising, not a buyer review.
TheRX daily service play threads list Scott Rickenbach, and Doc's Sports, under "Do not post these services".

VerifiedCappers shows 0 reviews, and the affiliate pages we opened (RideTheHotHand, Boyd's Bets, BetFirm) had no visible customer comments. Our Reddit library, harvested from r/sportsbook and r/sportsbetting through the Arctic Shift archive, holds no buyer post about him; live full text searches of the archive timed out. We found no BBB profile and no news coverage of complaints.

conflicts: Doc's Sports sells his packages, grades his picks and publishes his runs, so the store is also the scorekeeper.

RideTheHotHand states that it is "compensated by some of the services that the handicappers work with", and its link to his picks carries a partner ID. Boyd's Bets, BetFirm and Professional Sports Picks are reseller or affiliate pages.
The 2017 TheRX leaderboard post came from an account selling his packages.
strengths: A long and traceable career under one name and nickname, with an accounting background he states openly.
Low cost ways to try him: $25 to $30 one day packages, with store credit if the day loses.
Doc's Sports names its operator and a postal address, phone number and email.
His page breaks results down by sport, season and unit size, and the win rates we recomputed match the records shown.
No independent post we found accuses him of fraud or of failing to deliver picks.
concerns: Every number is graded by the store that sells him; no outside log of his paid picks exists that we could find.
Many records are slices by unit size or runs from unstated dates, and two different all sports runs (134-109 in July, 193-134 in November) are shown without start dates.
The guarantee pays only store credit or more picks, never cash, and the season packages carry no guarantee wording at all.
The only written buyer review we found was negative, though it is from 2011.
Several older outlets still show his name and prices though he no longer sells there, which can confuse buyers about where to buy.
checklist: Buy only on the Doc's Sports page that is live today; older affiliate pages may be out of date.
Ask Doc's Sports for every Rickenbach play from a fixed date, at every unit size, with the line and the time it was sent.
Check whether a quoted run starts on a date chosen after a hot streak.
Read the guarantee for the exact package: day packages give credit, longer ones give more picks, season packages show none.
Track the units you actually risk; a record of 7 unit plays says little about the 3 and 4 unit plays.
Remember that 52.4% is break even at -110 before you count the package price.
faq: He is a real handicapper who has sold picks under his own name for about two decades, now through Doc's Sports, which lists a Wisconsin postal address. Whether his picks win over time is not shown by any independent log; his posted records are graded by the store that sells him.
How much does Scott Rickenbach cost?

On 19 Nov 2026 Doc's Sports listed $25 to $30 for one day, $89 to $99 for a week, $279 to $325 for a month, $495 for the rest of the football season, and $795 to $850 for full basketball or hockey seasons, with regular prices of $950.
Does Scott Rickenbach have a verified record?
No. Doc's Sports shows runs such as 193-134 (+12,705) and a 2026 MLB season of 210-152, graded by itself. We found no third party log of his paid picks.
What is the Doc's Sports guarantee on his picks?

One day packages give a $25 or $30 account credit after a losing day, and some count a small profit as a loss. Weekly and monthly packages let you extend for free after a loss. We found no cash refund terms and no guarantee on season packages.
Where did Scott Rickenbach sell picks before Doc's Sports?

Older listings name his own company, Players Advantage, Inc, and Doc's Sports says he came from WagerTalk in 2025. Affiliate sites such as Boyd's Bets, BetFirm and Professional Sports Picks carried him in earlier years.

He shows detailed records and the cheapest packages carry store credit if they lose, but nothing we could open proves he beats the 52.4% needed at -110 over a fixed, full period. If you try him, start with one day and log every pick yourself.
